items.title: A framework of multilayer social networks for communication behavior with agent-based modeling
items.filename: A framework of multilayer social networks for communication behavior with agent-based modeling.md
items.summary: Proposes an agent-based framework combining multilayer social networks, a demographic-based population, and schedule-based behavior. It evaluates the framework by simulating H1N1 transmission in an artificial classroom and comparing it with a 2009 university outbreak; this is a general communication/network simulation rather than a social-media algorithm study.
items.reason: Directly models communication behavior over multilayer social ties, but the application is classroom influenza transmission and does not address platform algorithms, belief models, or social integration.
items.entry: vault/Literature/Papers/Entries/A framework of multilayer social networks for communication behavior with agent-based modeling.md

items.title: Agent-Based Modeling and Simulation of Collaborative Social Networks
items.filename: Agent-Based Modeling and Simulation of Collaborative Social Networks.md
items.summary: Models open-source software developers as agents in a collaborative social network, where developers may create, join, or abandon projects or continue collaborations. The application concerns collaborative software development, not social-media feed algorithms.
items.reason: Agent-based simulation of collaborative social ties and their evolution offers a relevant network modeling precedent, though its agents and setting are developer-project collaborations.
items.entry: vault/Literature/Papers/Entries/Agent-Based Modeling and Simulation of Collaborative Social Networks.md

items.title: Agent-based modeling: Methods and techniques for simulating human systems
items.filename: Agent-based modeling - Methods and techniques for simulating human systems.md
items.publication: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 99(suppl 3), 7280–7287
items.summary: A methodological overview of agent-based modeling for human systems. It discusses when ABM is useful, including heterogeneous agents, complex interactions, heterogeneous network topology, and adaptation, alongside issues of purpose, calibration, validation, and interpretation.
items.reason: General ABM methods provide background but do not directly simulate social-media algorithms or the thesis's specific integration mechanisms.
items.entry: vault/Literature/Papers/Entries/Agent-based modeling - Methods and techniques for simulating human systems.md

items.title: Agent-Based Simulation Models in Organization Science
items.filename: Agent-Based Simulation Models in Organization Science.md
items.summary: Discusses agent-based simulation of interactions between members of organizations or between organizations, including applications to organization science and an introductory guide to simulation platforms.
items.reason: General methodological introduction with organizational applications; no direct treatment of online platforms, algorithmic recommendations, or social integration.
